This smart, resonant and solidly entertaining production was worth the wait.

An immensely entertaining Radio Golf, the final play by the late great playwright August Wilson has arrived on Broadway in a handsomely staged production by Kenny Leon that bristles with forceful urgency.
Radio Golf 's weaknesses don't diminish Wilson's full chronicle, and its strengths more than justify it as a highly fitting finale to one of American theatre's most estimable epics.

cn.t: Wilson's final play in his 10-play cycle arrives on Broadway as a smart, resonant, and solidly entertaining work. Critics praise its compelling story, forceful urgency, and outstanding cast of five delivering a handsomely staged production.

vs.sum: A beautifully restored theater with a stunning Tiffany-inspired interior. The 2021 renovation transformed restroom facilities from among Broadway's worst to a model for the industry, with modern bathrooms on every public level.

acc.note: Elevator to Mezzanine, Balcony, and lower level restrooms. 7 wheelchair spaces across all levels.
